parole.testo: Akin to Danish flot (“nice, pleasant, cool”), both borrowed from Low German vlot. Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *fleutaną (“to stream, float”). See also German flott (“stylish, charming”).
Borrowed from Low German agurke, borrowed via Polish from Greek αγγούρι (angoúri, “cucumber”).

parole.significato: ham (a cured leg of a swine, or other similar cured pork)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Low German schinke, from Middle Low German schinke, from Old Saxon skinka, from Proto-West Germanic *skinkō. Cognate with Swedish skinka. In relation to the tanning sense, compare Japanese ガングロ (ganguro, literally “black face”).
Borrowed from Low German wesen, compare with Danish væsen.
